title: The Right’s Strategy to Destabilize Mexico; the American Society Case
author: Nancy Flores
content:
_This article by Nancy Flores originally appeared in the[July 23, 2026 edition
of Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/la-estrategia-de-la-
derecha-para-desestabilizar-mexico-caso-american-society/), a Mexican
investigative journalism magazine._

In recent weeks, one of the most relevant bets of the Mexican and
international right was to accelerate its strategy of political, economic, and
social destabilization of Mexico in the context of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
Its objective was to try to prevent it from being held in Mexico City and to
take advantage of that sporting event to encourage narratives associated with
the "narco-government" campaigns and foreign distrust, of both investment and
tourists.

As at other moments, its main tool has been to spread lies through the media
corporations and social networks. The false crisis scenarios, however, did not
work out for them: the matches played in the capital went off without
problems; the Fan Fest in the Zócalo was a success, and sports fans did not
associate their disappointment over the Mexican national team's defeat with
the government's performance.

In that same context, their calls on the US government for Donald Trump to
intervene in the country did not work either. The World Cup unfolded without
incident and the month of June was one of the most peaceful in the country,
with a 48 percent drop in intentional homicides, according to the federal
Security Cabinet.

Despite these failures, the right's destabilization campaigns continue. And
one of the most active agents has been the American Society organization,
Mexico chapter. Headed by the Mexican-American right-winger Larry Rubin, the
association called a dinner this past June 6, attended by politicians opposed
to the 4T, as well as representatives of the media corporations.

The dinner, whose explicit objective was for Mexicans to celebrate the 250th
anniversary of the founding of the United States, was the epicenter of the
destabilizing strategy; this, despite the fact that it did not have the
physical presence of Ambassador Ronald Johnson, who was considered the "guest
of honor."

Days earlier, on May 31, President Claudia Sheinbaum denounced, at the
Monument to the Revolution and before more than 100,000 attendees, the worst
media onslaught her government has faced, and defended national sovereignty in
the face of foreign interference. This, after the US government requested the
urgent arrest of the now governor on leave of Sinaloa, Rubén Rocha Moya, and
nine other people, allegedly linked to the Los Chapitos case.

At the dinner that brought together the Mexican-American right, Larry Rubin
said, among other things, that Mexico and the United States should have a real
TLCC, which he described as a "crime-fighting treaty" for binational security,
with an approach that once again fed the narrative that President Sheinbaum's
government does nothing to combat drug trafficking, and that Donald Trump's
administration does.

On June 8, at her morning press conference, the head of the Executive
criticized that the dinner not only brought together the PRIAN, but also
businesspeople associated with the right. In this regard, she stressed that
the meeting was financed by Grupo Salinas and used by opposition politicians
to ask for US government intervention in Mexico's internal affairs.

By June 9, Larry Rubin rejected that the American Society of Mexico is a
platform against the Mexican government, and affirmed that the objective is to
"strengthen" the bilateral relationship with the United States. A month later,
during a radio interview, Rubin insisted on his TLCC proposal and criticized
President Sheinbaum for upholding the defense of sovereignty. From his point
of view, the US agencies are not the "enemy," but rather the criminal groups,
despite the recent history involving the DEA, the FBI, and the CIA in
clandestine operations in Mexico, in frank violation of our laws
(Constitution, National Security Law) and of the international law that
establishes respect for the self-determination of peoples as a principle.

### Spokespeople Linked to the American Society of Mexico

On several occasions, Larry Rubin has said that because of his dual
nationality he speaks of "his country" interchangeably: he can be referring to
the United States or to Mexico. The truth is that, given the way he acts and
the interests he defends, it is obvious that the current president of the
American Society of Mexico identifies more with the neighboring country to the
north than with Mexican nationality. Otherwise, he would defend the homeland
above any other country.

Despite being the most visible face of the American Society of Mexico, Rubin
is not the only voice linked to that organization that feeds the US
government's interventionist narratives. There is also the media participation
of the "political analyst" Gricha Raether, who on March 8, 2025 declared to
the press that the business community knew that Trump's imposition of tariffs
"was the fault of the narco-government in Mexico," the same narrative pushed
by the US agencies.

Alongside Larry Rubin, the 4T opponent Gricha Raether is a member of the Board
of Directors of the American Society of Mexico and secretary general of the
[unregistered] party México Republicano. In his media appearances he has
defended Donald Trump's anti-immigrant policies, based on the idea that the
United States should deport criminals and terrorists.

The México Republicano party is Trumpist in orientation, and prior to
Raether's arrival it was headed by Juan Iván Peña Nader, who was coordinator
of advisors to the Deputy Secretary of Government at the Interior Ministry,
Abraham Kunio González, during the Felipe Calderón administration. He is also
chief payment officer of Mis Métricas, SAPI de CV, a meal-voucher contractor.

In turn, Raether is associated with another 4T opponent who is very active in
media and social networks: Ghaleb Krame, a former collaborator of the PRI ex-
governor of Veracruz, Javier Duarte, imprisoned on corruption charges, who has
positioned himself as an "expert voice" on security issues in most of Mexico's
media corporations.

An open opponent of the Sheinbaum government, following the life sentence of
drug trafficker Ismael "el Mayo" Zambada, Ghaleb Krame suggested that the
Sinaloa Cartel leader sent a political message by indicating that he was not
cooperating with US prosecutors nor accusing any official. According to Krame,
that message was destined for Palenque, where former President Andrés Manuel
López Obrador resides, or the National Palace, seat of the federal government.

Although Krame describes himself as an academic and an expert in national
security and policing, his track record in PRI and PAN governments accused of
corruption is his true calling card. In Veracruz he was a collaborator, first,
of Fidel Herrera; and then of Javier Duarte. In the latter case, he was
director general of Institutional Liaison and Crime Prevention and executive
secretary of the Interinstitutional Commission for the Social Prevention of
Violence and Crime, between 2011 and 2015. The security expert seems to have
forgotten that his former boss Javier Duarte remains imprisoned for criminal
association and money laundering.

![2014 IPAX document naming Ghaleb Krame as a director in Javier Duarte's
Veracruz government](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/02-annotated.jpg)The IPAX document (2014)

In addition, between 2016 and 2017, Krame collaborated with José Ignacio
Peralta Sánchez, former governor of Colima. In that government he was deputy
secretary of Crime Prevention and Citizen Participation. His former boss,
Peralta Sánchez, was bound over for trial for embezzlement and misuse of
powers.

And the jewel in the crown: Krame was a collaborator of the PAN member
Francisco Javier García Cabeza de Vaca, in Tamaulipas. Between 2017 and 2018
he was coordinator of advisors to the head of Police Strategy at the SSP and
interim deputy secretary of Sentence Execution and Social Reintegration,
following the murder of Felipe Javier Téllez. As is known, García Cabeza de
Vaca has an arrest warrant against him for alleged organized crime and money
laundering.

![Instagram post by García Cabeza de Vaca posing with Ghaleb Krame in Miami,
December 2025](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/03-annotated.jpg)The Miami photo (Instagram, December
11, 2025)

Despite that background and those friendships, Ghaleb Krame opines as an
"expert voice" in the media on public security and criticizes the policies of
the Fourth Transformation, in line with the position of the American Society
of Mexico. And on his social networks he labels President Sheinbaum's
administration the "narco-government," in tune with the vision that the US DEA
seeks to impose.

![X post by Ghaleb Krame calling Mexico a narco-government while Morena
remains in power](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/04-annotated.jpg)The “narco-government” post (X,
January 21, 2026)

Added to his political interests are his business interests, as he is a
partner in three companies: Krame & Raether, SA de CV, where he is associated
with Gricha Raether; KRC Intelligence Group, SA de CV; and Gutbar Servicios
Empresariales, SA de CV.

![Network diagram of Ghaleb Krame's companies and
connections](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/05-annotated-scaled.jpg)The network map

In KRC Intelligence Group he is a partner of Humberto Romero Gudiño; and in
Gutbar Servicios Empresariales, SA de CV, he is a partner of Alejandro Ariel
Peña Merodio, who, as director general of the Cancún Auxiliary Police,
drunkenly threatened a journalist with death.
